Issued at 206 PM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Rest of Today-Friday...High pressure over the Great Lakes builds 
eastward through the end of the work week, nudging an upper level 
trough through the Florida peninsula. Onshore flow persists through 
the period, aided by departing Subtropical Storm Josephine and a 
stalled front over the northern Caribbean. A tightening pressure 
gradient will lead to increasingly breezy conditions, with NE winds 
10-15 mph this afternoon becoming 15-20 mph Friday. Widespread gusts 
20-25 mph are forecast Friday afternoon, occasionally up to 30 mph 
along the coast. Onshore flow will keep high temperatures near 
normal, in the lower 80s. However, Atlantic waters in the 70s will 
keep overnight low temperatures in the upper 60s along the coast, 
while inland temperatures dip into the upper 50s to lower 60s.

Early morning showers along the Treasure Coast have diminished by 
early afternoon. Will likely see drier conditions prevail through 
the daytime hours, though can't rule out a shower or two (20%) 
moving onshore into that area through sundown. Overall, available 
moisture remains relatively low compared to the last several weeks 
(PWATs 1.2" or less). However, with upper level support from the 
trough, CAMs suggest scattered showers developing overnight 
offshore. Rain chances increase northward into Friday night, with 
the highest chances remaining along the coast (30-50%). Inland areas 
look to stay mostly dry. The thunder threat appears low (below 20%) 
thanks to subsidence in the mid-levels. Will need to monitor the 
threat for training bands of showers, leading to minor flooding. 
Portions of the Treasure Coast remain in a Marginal Risk (1/4) for 
excessive rainfall.

Saturday-Wednesday...High pressure strengthens over the eastern
half of the US, well north of the Florida peninsula, through early
next week. Meanwhile, an area of low pressure looks to develop
over the Atlantic NE of the Bahamas along the stalled frontal
boundary south of the state. The pressure gradient will become 
increasingly tight between these two features, enhancing already 
breezy onshore flow, beginning this weekend. NE winds 15-20 mph, 
with gusts 30-40 mph, on Saturday continue to increase Sunday and 
into Monday, becoming 20-25 mph, with gusts 35-45 mph. The highest
gusts are forecast along the coast, where Wind Advisories appear 
likely. Breezy to windy low looks to linger into mid-week next 
week, though Sunday and Monday appear to be the windiest days.

Confidence is increasing that this prolonged period of strong 
onshore flow will coincide with the highest set of king tides for
the year, meaning that coastal impacts will be exacerbated 
compared to the onshore flow event last weekend. Dangerous beach 
and boating conditions are forecast, with minor to moderate 
coastal flooding around high tide, moderate to locally major beach
erosion, and high, pounding surf up to 12-15 ft. Residents and 
visitors are urged to stay out of the water and to even use 
caution on the beach itself, especially near periods of high tide.

Rain chances also look to increase this weekend, as moisture
rebounds (PWATs return to 1.5"+). Multiple rounds of gusty,
onshore moving showers are expected. Thus, the highest chances (up
to 80% on Sunday) are forecast for coastal areas, though
occasionally showers may persist into inland locations. Areas that
see multiple rounds of rainfall or any training bands could see
increased flooding concerns. At this time, the Treasure Coast
looks to be the greatest threat area, which is highlighted under a
Marginal Risk (1/4) for excessive rainfall each day. High
temperatures remain near normal, in the lower 80s, with warmer
overnight lows in the lower 70s along the coast and mid to upper
60s inland.
